details.summary: A highly practical, delicious, and perfectly aligned weeknight dinner that requires only a minor tweak to the preheating language to be ready for print.

dimensions.feedback: Classic and perfectly coherent flavor profile. Lemon, dill, mustard, and salmon are a timeless, reliable combination.
All ingredients in the list are accurately accounted for in the instruction steps.

The instruction 'Preheat the oven to 425°F / 220°C for 5 minutes' is confusing, as ovens take varying times to preheat. Simply state 'Preheat the oven to 425°F / 220°C.' Additionally, direct the reader to lightly toss the green beans in the pan's residual oil when adding them so they do not roast completely dry.
Aligns seamlessly with the Mediterranean-American style, utilizing olive oil, fresh herbs, and wholesome ingredients.
Sheet-pan roasting at 425°F works excellently. Staggering the cooking times (potatoes first, then salmon and beans) ensures everything finishes beautifully without overcooking the fish.
The computed nutrition panel accurately reflects the ingredients and quantities provided.
Title and intro are inviting, accurate, and completely free of disallowed health claims or 'diet' framing.
A highly appealing, practical weeknight dinner. It offers a great mix of textures and bright, vibrant colors on the plate.
An excellent example of the book's dual-action philosophy: skin-on potatoes for quality complex carbs and fiber, ample greens, and omega-3 rich salmon.
Zero added sugar, and the potatoes provide 46.6g of high-quality carbohydrates, landing the meal perfectly within the targeted carbohydrate window for stable blood sugar.
Hits the Fish & Seafood Main nutrient targets flawlessly and delivers on the promise of an easy weeknight seafood meal.
Very realistic for a 30-minute timeframe. Chopping baby potatoes and trimming beans takes about 8 minutes, leaving 22 minutes for the staggered roast.
